reasons: The data is hand-typed with no source dates.
Only part of the file is in this packet, so the LNG lists and the industry lookup could not be checked.

terms.meaning: engineering, procurement and construction: firms that design, buy equipment for and build a plant
liquefied natural gas, gas cooled to a liquid so it can be shipped
another name a company is known by, such as a former name or a short form
a government-backed body that insures or lends money for exports

sections.name: PackCompany
sections.title: Shape of one company entry
sections.what: Describes one company record: its ID, name, type, country, website and other known names. Every company list in this file uses this same shape.
sections.why: Likely reason: the other known names help recognize one company under several names. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Nothing here stops two records from sharing an ID, so a duplicate ID would go unnoticed.

sections.name: CompanyPack
sections.title: Shape of one company pack
sections.what: Describes a named group of companies, such as operators or engineering firms, with its own short description and a count.
sections.why: Likely reason: the app shows companies in named groups. Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: operators
sections.title: Nuclear plant operators list
sections.what: A hand-written list of more than 50 nuclear plant owners and operators from many countries, each typed as owner operator. Examples include EDF, KEPCO and CNNC.
sections.why: Likely reason: a reference list of who runs nuclear plants, used to name companies in the nuclear packs. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The entries are typed by hand with no source or check date, so a company that changed its name or owner stays wrong until someone edits it.

sections.name: epcContractors
sections.title: Nuclear engineering and construction firms list
sections.what: A hand-written list of about 30 engineering, procurement and construction firms, each typed as EPC, such as Bechtel, AtkinsRealis and Hyundai E&C.
sections.why: Likely reason: separates firms that build plants from firms that run them. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Some firms share a website with another entry, such as the two Doosan records, so the website alone cannot tell them apart.

sections.name: vendors
sections.title: Reactor vendors and technology list
sections.what: A hand-written list of about 25 reactor designers and technology suppliers, each typed as technology provider. It includes Westinghouse, Framatome, Rosatom and several smaller reactor developers.
sections.why: Likely reason: separates companies that design reactors from those that build or run plants. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Some aliases are short or common, such as Doosan or Toshiba, so a text match on them could point to the wrong company.

sections.name: developers
sections.title: Developers and national labs list
sections.what: A hand-written list of about 30 project developers and national research laboratories, typed as developer. It mixes project companies, such as Sizewell C Company, with research bodies, such as Oak Ridge National Laboratory.
sections.why: The pack description calls these project developers and labs. The reason for mixing the two is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Research laboratories are not companies that build plants, so counts or searches of developers will include them unless they are filtered out.

sections.name: financialBackers
sections.title: Financial backers and export credit agencies list
sections.what: A hand-written list of about 30 banks, export credit agencies and development lenders, each typed as financial backer. Each institution gets one country, which is its home country, so the World Bank is listed under the United States.
sections.why: Likely reason: groups the institutions that fund or insure projects. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The single country given to multilateral lenders is a choice the code does not explain, so it may mislead a reader about where they operate.

sections.name: NUCLEAR_COMPANY_PACKS
sections.title: Nuclear packs grouping the lists
sections.what: Groups the five nuclear lists into named packs: operators and utilities, engineering and construction, reactor vendors, developers and labs, and financial backers. Each pack has a description and a count worked out from its list.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the app show nuclear companies in a few clear groups. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The descriptions contain typed numbers such as 45 plus more, which will not update when the lists change.

sections.name: lngOperators
sections.title: LNG operators list
sections.what: A hand-written list of about 20 liquefied natural gas owners, operators and developers, such as QatarEnergy, Cheniere and Shell, each with a type, country and website. These are the base for the LNG packs in the part of the file not shown here.
sections.why: The file header says these are real organizations with stable top-level web addresses. The reason for keeping LNG separate is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Several aliases are plant or project names, such as Sabine Pass Liquefaction, and a common word such as Total could match unrelated text.

sections.name: lngEpc
sections.title: Known LNG construction contractors list
sections.what: A fixed list of ten firms that build LNG plants, each with a name, country, website and other names they are known by. It feeds the contractor group of the LNG pack.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the sector's known companies in code so the app can show them without a database.
sections.watch_out: The ids are fixed text; if other data refers to them, renaming one breaks that link, and this section does not show whether anything does.

sections.name: lngTechnology
sections.title: Known LNG technology and equipment suppliers list
sections.what: A fixed list of nine companies that license liquefaction processes or supply key equipment for LNG plants, in the same format as the contractor list.
sections.why: Likely reason: same purpose as the contractor list, for the technology group.
sections.watch_out: Entries are typed by hand with no source link, so a wrong country or website would be shown as fact.

sections.name: lngShipping
sections.title: Known LNG shipping and shipyard companies list
sections.what: A fixed list of ten shipowners and shipbuilders linked to LNG carriers. Every entry is labelled SUPPLIER, although some are ship owners rather than suppliers.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The single SUPPLIER label does not separate owners from shipyards, so any filter on the type field will mix them.

sections.name: LNG_COMPANY_PACKS
sections.title: LNG company packs grouped by role
sections.what: Bundles the four LNG groups (operators and developers, contractors, technology, shipping) into the list shape the app uses, each with a count and a short description. The counts are calculated from the lists, while the descriptions are typed by hand.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the app show each group with its size and summary from one structure.
sections.watch_out: The descriptions name example companies by hand, so they can drift from the lists when a list changes.

sections.name: COMPANY_PACKS_BY_INDUSTRY
sections.title: Industry lookup table for company packs
sections.what: Maps each industry key, nuclear or lng, to its company pack list. Industries missing from this table have no packs yet.
sections.why: The comment in the code states the rule: an industry with no entry shows an honest empty state and never falls back to nuclear content.
sections.watch_out: A new industry needs a new line here using the exact key the app uses; a mismatch silently shows nothing.

sections.name: getCompanyPacksForIndustry
sections.title: Safe lookup of packs by industry
sections.what: Returns the company packs for a given industry key, or an empty list when the key is unknown.
sections.why: Likely reason: returns an empty list instead of an error so the caller can show an empty state.
sections.watch_out: A typo in the industry key returns an empty list with no error, so it looks like missing data.

summary: A hand-typed reference list of nuclear and LNG companies, sorted into named groups with their type, country, website and other known names.
purpose: Gives the app a fixed set of company records to show, group or match against.
why: Likely reason: a curated list keeps company information consistent across the app. Reason not stated in the code.
how: Defines separate lists of nuclear owners and operators, engineering firms, technology vendors, developers and labs, and financial backers. Groups the nuclear lists into five named packs. The lower part of the file, not shown in this packet, adds the LNG lists, the LNG packs, and a lookup by industry.
inputs: No runtime inputs. The records are typed into the file.
outputs: Exported company packs and records for other code to use. The code that reads them is not in this packet.
risks: The data is hand-entered with no source or check date, so entries can be wrong or out of date. Shared websites and short aliases may cause mismatches. Counts typed into descriptions can drift from the real lists.
debug: If a company is missing or wrong, search this file for its name or an alias. If a count in a description looks off, compare it with the list length. If a link is wrong, check that company's website field.
